publicReleaseNotes: Lamp 1.6.0 adds Sorry move-in, from authenticated exports or keyless public JSON, preserving components, grouping, notice timelines, maintenance and old public paths; Sorry email subscribers stay held through hostname cutover until the owner releases their confirmation invitations. Managed hosting can send mail through RER with durable incident threading (migration 0026), alongside Resend and SendGrid. A redeploy keeps each Worker's SESSION_SECRET, SUBSCRIBER_TOKEN_SECRET and WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET, so emailed Manage and Unsubscribe links and operator sessions keep working; LAMP_REPLACE_SECRETS rotates one on purpose. Subscribers choose components on the subscribe form, and both the form and the management page keep exactly the boxes ticked. Unsubscribing restores the address's confirmation allowance, so re-subscribing sends a fresh confirmation. Deliveries lists confirmation and other subscription email; setup pages for identity providers, monitoring presets, Slack and Teams can be finished on the page; a build never carries local settings files. The checkout pins rer 0.2.36. Product screenshot: .github/assets/release/lamp-1.6.0-status-page-1440.png (a business's public status page at 1440 pixels: grouped components with 90-day uptime, a resolved incident and the subscribe form's component choice).

MOVE-001.summary: Sorry adds authenticated saved/API reads and keyless public previews to the reviewed import flow.
MOVE-001.was: Dry run first: An owner moving from Statuspage, Better Stack or Instatus gives Settings → Move in either an API key with its page ID (read once with GET requests to the source's fixed API origin, never stored) or the source's saved API responses. A dry run counts every component, component group, incident with its updates, scheduled maintenance and subscriber as imported, changed, skipped or refused, names each reason, and writes nothing. An import applies only the reviewed dry run: if the source or this page changed since, it is refused and a fresh dry run is required.
MOVE-001.now: Dry run first: An owner moving from Statuspage, Better Stack, Instatus or Sorry gives Settings → Move in either an API key with its page ID (read once with GET requests to the source's fixed API origin, never stored) or the source's saved API responses. A dry run counts every component, component group, incident with its updates, scheduled maintenance and subscriber as imported, changed, skipped or refused, names each reason, and writes nothing. An import applies only the reviewed dry run: if the source or this page changed since, it is refused and a fresh dry run is required.

MOVE-002.summary: Sorry subscriber candidates remain inert through cutover; explicit release starts their confirmation window.
MOVE-002.was: Retroactive and silent: An import keeps every incident update's original publication time and derives each imported component's state history from those times, as INCIDENT-009 does; it queues no notification for any incident or maintenance and publishes no maintenance notice. A window already over is imported as completed. Each imported email subscriber is pending. Preview, apply, resume, job reads and Cutover checks send no mail. Only the authenticated owner’s explicit Send invitations action claims and sends each eligible pending email subscriber at most one confirmation invitation, mentioning no past incident. Confirmation expires 72 hours from the import review time stored as created_at, even when sending is delayed; expired subscribers cannot be invited and SUB-003 deletes unconfirmed addresses. A claim precedes the transport call to prevent duplicates across concurrent batches and retries. Proven preparation failures remain retryable because no message was submitted; interrupted or uncertain claimed sends are not automatically retried.

MOVE-005.summary: Sorry notice IDs, exact supplied links and history paths resolve on the moved hostname.
MOVE-005.was: Old public addresses: Imported incident and maintenance source paths and supplied shortlink paths permanently redirect on the public host to each surviving record's Lamp permalink; maintenance has its own permanent page. Source Atom paths (`/history.atom` for Statuspage and Instatus; `/feed.atom` for Better Stack) serve Lamp's Atom feed after import, even without incident history, until a complete undo removes the import. These responses come from the same versioned snapshot as the page, without database queries. A second apply duplicates no aliases; conditional undo removes exactly the removed records' aliases and keeps preserved records' aliases. New imports refuse and name unsafe addresses, native-path collisions and conflicting destinations; an older retained source reports unusable aliases without withholding the public snapshot. Missing shortlinks are never invented. Source-owned shortlink hostnames remain outside Lamp's control. Better Stack REST reports supply no documented public URL; their paths are unavailable unless an unchanged saved status-page webhook supplies an exact shortlink with a matching report ID. No `/incident/<REST-id>` path is guessed. Better Stack maintenance messages are retained as historical updates, without creating native lifecycle notices or replaying notifications.

Sorry numeric notice and supplied notice paths redirect to the matching incident or maintenance; `/notices` and `/history/` redirect to Lamp’s `/history`. MOVE-006.summary: Sorry cutover records the live configured hostname and closed watch window before invitations.
MOVE-006.was: Cutover preview: Settings → Cutover is available after a dry run and for saved imports. It shows up to the first 25 old incident and maintenance addresses with proposed or surviving native permalinks, unavailable addresses and source-host limits, source feed answers, unsupported JSON/RSS/widget consumers, and eligible invitations with their original expiry deadline. Once the owner selects a public origin, each Opens check uses a credentialless browser request that follows the redirect and verifies the final native address and successful HTML response; failures remain explicit. The ordered guide covers import, preview, explicit invitations, hostname/custom-domain instructions, rechecking and keeping the source through the confirmation window. It claims neither DNS validation nor inbox delivery. Instatus accepts its documented saved management REST response families with a separate owner acknowledgement that the page and supplied history are published and unrestricted. Known protected or unpublished source records cannot become public. Visual Component parents are groups; audience groups are refused access restrictions. Only confirmed, approved email-only subscriptions with resolved preferences become pending. Exact supplied public-summary incident/maintenance URLs are joined by source ID; missing URLs are not invented. Maintenance ends use explicit timestamps or documented duration minutes under completed/autoEnd semantics, with every update retained silently.

Only confirmed, approved email-only subscriptions with resolved preferences become pending. Exact supplied public-summary incident/maintenance URLs are joined by source ID; missing URLs are not invented. Maintenance ends use explicit timestamps or documented duration minutes under completed/autoEnd semantics, with every update retained silently. Sorry general notices may have no affected component and are carried as resolved informational history without outage claims; cancelled maintenance stays cancelled. Sorry additionally accepts keyless public JSON captures, including paginated components and notices plus full detail for every notice. Partial public previews name uncaptured details and cannot be applied. Subscribers come only from the authenticated API; eligible email rows are held inert without mail or confirmation expiry. After the hostname is live and the watch window closes, an explicit owner invitation action names the configured public origin, records that approval, and releases held rows into pending with a 72-hour window starting at release. Undo cannot recall mail or remove a released row as if it were still unchanged. Sorry numeric notice IDs and supplied notice paths redirect to surviving Lamp incidents or maintenance; `/notices` and `/history/` redirect to Lamp’s `/history`.

SUB-001.summary: Unsubscribing through an emailed link restores the address's confirmation allowance, so re-subscribing sends a fresh confirmation.
SUB-001.was: Submitting an email address on the public page creates a pending subscription and sends one confirmation email to that address within 60 seconds. That address receives at most one confirmation email in any 24 hours however many times it is submitted, which is what bounds a subscription-bombing attack. A pending subscription receives no other notification. The form is a standard POST that works with script disabled, is rejected with 403 when the request carries `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, and carries no CSRF token, because with no cookie and no session there is no ambient authority to forge.
SUB-001.now: Submitting an email address on the public page creates a pending subscription and sends one confirmation email to that address within 60 seconds. That address receives at most one confirmation email in any 24 hours however many times it is submitted, which is what bounds a subscription-bombing attack. Unsubscribing through a link emailed to the address proves it is the subscriber's own and restores that allowance, so re-subscribing after unsubscribing sends a fresh confirmation. A pending subscription receives no other notification. The form is a standard POST that works with script disabled, is rejected with 403 when the request carries `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, and carries no CSRF token, because with no cookie and no session there is no ambient authority to forge.

SUB-004.summary: Subscribers choose components on the subscribe form as well as the management page, and both keep exactly the ticked components.
SUB-004.was: A subscriber selects which components they want updates about, and is notified about an incident or maintenance only when it claims a state for at least one component in that selection. A subscription whose selection has never been narrowed follows every visible component, including components added after it was created. A subscription with a narrowed selection is unchanged when a component is added. When a component is attached to an unresolved incident, every subscriber who follows that component and has received no notification for that incident receives exactly one notification carrying its most recent published update, and then receives subsequent updates normally.
SUB-004.now: A subscriber selects which components they want updates about, on the subscribe form or later on the management page, and the subscription follows exactly the components ticked (none ticked follows all), and is notified about an incident or maintenance only when it claims a state for at least one component in that selection. A subscription whose selection has never been narrowed follows every visible component, including components added after it was created. A subscription with a narrowed selection is unchanged when a component is added. When a component is attached to an unresolved incident, every subscriber who follows that component and has received no notification for that incident receives exactly one notification carrying its most recent published update, and then receives subsequent updates normally.

migrations.buyerSteps: Apply this additive migration before starting the updated Worker. It records owner-approved Sorry subscriber releases; no prior import or subscription is changed.
Apply before starting the updated Worker. Adds a message-key index to retain Managed relay thread receipts; direct provider behavior is unchanged.

agentUpdateInstructions: Back up data and owner source. Apply 0025_sorry_import_release.sql and then 0026_managed_mail_threads.sql before starting the updated Worker; both are additive and change no existing row, and the complete release history is retained. Redeploys now keep the signing secrets a Worker already holds; set LAMP_REPLACE_SECRETS=NAME[,NAME] only to rotate one deliberately, which invalidates the links or sessions it signs. Keep supplying the original secrets when restoring into a new installation. For Sorry, review original saved responses or a keyless public capture, apply only the reviewed fingerprint, move the configured hostname and close the observation window before explicitly releasing held subscribers. Release begins their 72-hour confirmation window. Keep the incumbent available through confirmation; undo cannot recall sent mail. Existing Statuspage, Better Stack and Instatus confirmation deadlines are unchanged. Run rer verify and pnpm run verify:release from v1.5.1 before adopting.
